turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. Who decided to give Owen a zero, and when?

I have six things. One, the version history: created October 28 at 11:31 PM, 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58, no earlier drafts. Two, the essay quotes a line from Act 3, Scene 2 that is not in Hamlet. Three, his October 15 outline argued cowardice; the essay never mentions it. Four, on November 2 he could not tell me what epistemological paralysis means. Five, his in-class writing on September 24 was 380 words with comma splices and no quotations. Six, the checker said 94 percent.

Your sixth is a machine's guess, and the company that sells it says it shouldn't be the sole basis for anything. Put that Act 3, Scene 2 line in front of me, next to the play. And none of the six explains why nobody called me before the zero went in.
Which of those do you want to see first?
The line from the essay, and the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. Now.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero withdrawn, an apology for entering it before anyone contacted me, the Act 3, Scene 2 line from Owen's essay set beside the play, and a guarantee that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position and agreed to nothing; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and to see the misquoted line checked against the play. The fair outcome is a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and the meeting ended before any evidence was put in front of her.
What moved her: Nothing, because you described six pieces of evidence but never showed her one she could check.
What cost ground: You laid out all six at once with the checker score among them, which gave her an easy target and let her brush past the stronger items.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your version history put the essay's creation late on the night before it was due, which landed close to that kind of night and right where she was weakest. It proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked for the Act 3, Scene 2 line beside the play, put it in front of her right then instead of asking which item she wanted first, and leave the checker score out entirely.
